text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police shoot dead two Kenyatta University students a day after another student was killed by a policeman during a riot.
- Ailing dissident Koigi wa Wamwere will travel to Oslo, Norway on Thursday night to receive medical treatment.
- More than 13,000 bank workers threaten to go on strike until the sacking of their union's chief shop steward is revoked.
- Murdered in cold blood! Police gun down two more students.
- Kenya's government condemns a report attributed to Zaire's information minister over the heads of state summit on the Great Lakes crisis in Nairobi.
- Opposition Democratic Party of Kenya says it will oppose the start of voters registration until all eligible Kenyans are issued with the new generation identity cards.
- A row over Nairobi's birth date threatens to plunge the city's 100th anniversary celebrations scheduled for Friday into confusion.
- Six Nigerians are charged before a Nairobi chief magistrate with trafficking heroin.
- The Italian Trade Commission closes its office in Kenya amid protests from local employees over their termination benefits.
